newsitem.title: USA: Marvel Holding Cos files for Chapter 11.
newsitem.headline: Marvel Holding Cos files for Chapter 11.

text.p: Marvel Holdings, Marvel (Parent) Holdings and Marvel III Holdings said on Friday they filed voluntary petitions for reorganization under Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code in a Delaware court.
The three holdings companies said they owned about 80.2 million shares of Marvel Entertainment Group Inc common stock.
In a separate statement, Marvel Entertainment Group Inc said on Friday it filed a voluntary petition for reorganization in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware in Wilmington, Del.

It said it filed the petition in order to carry out a proposed $525 million recapitalization plan that would enable Marvel to pursue its new strategic intitiatives and achieve sustained profitability.
Marvel Entertainment also said the filing would ensure it could continue business operations without interruption while it obtained approvals of its financial restructuring plan.
Financier Ronald Perelman's Andrews Group Inc controls Marvel and owns about 80 percent of its stock.
Marvel Holdings Inc has $121 million in assets, based on its ownership of 51 million shares of Marvel Entertainment, and $517.4 million in liabilities, according to court documents.
The Bank of New York is a trustee for the senior secured discount notes due 1998 and the series B senior secured discount notes due 1998, according to court documents.
The debt is secured by 48 million of Marvel Holding's 51 million Marvel Entertainment shares, according to court papers.
Marvel Holdings Vice President Glenn Dickes said, "The value of the collateral is significantly less than the value of debt secured by collateral."
Marvel Entertainment has $229.6 million in assets and $693.2 million in liabilities, according to court papers.
Of those liabilities, $630.7 million is contingent secured debt and $58.2 million is fixed liquidated unsecured debt, according to court papers.
In a separate statement, Andrews Group said it signed a defitive merger agreement to acquire all Class A shares of Toy Biz Inc common stock held by Toy Biz public stockholders for $22.50 per share.
Marvel owns all of the Toy Biz Class B stock.
But Andrews said the deal would depend on Marvel Entertainment Group Inc's plan of reorganization.

As part of that plan, Andrews Group said it would acquire from Marvel for $365 million in cash or Toy Biz Class A common stock or a combination of these, newly issued shares of Marvel common stock representing 80.8 percent of the outstanding shares of Marvel common stock after giving effect to the acquisition.
In effect, Andrews was making an equity investment in Marvel Entertainment in exchange for newly issued shares.

On November 20, Andrews agreed to buy the 67 percent of Toy Biz shares held by Isaac Perlmutter and Avi Arad for aobut $17 per share. At that time, it proposed buying the remaining Class A shares for $22.50 per share, the group said.
But a special committee of Toy Biz's board backed a deal under which Andrews would purchase these remaining Class A shares for $22.50 per share, the group said in December.

If the reorganization plan was confirmed, Andrews said on Friday it expected to assign its rights and obligations under the Toy Biz merger agreement to Marvel and that Toy Biz would become a wholly-owned subsidiary of Marvel.
